The '''1931 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship''' was the 45th staging of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]'s premier [[inter county|inter-county]] [[hurling]] tournament. The championship ran from 10 May to 1 November 1931.

[[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] were the [[1930 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|defending champions]], however, they were beaten by [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the [[#Munster semi-finals|Munster semi-final]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/county/wexford/enniscorthy-news/a-collection-of-tipperary-gaa-ballads/a/149763745.html|title=A collection of Tipperary GAA ballads|publisher=Irish Independent|date=5 June 1990|accessdate=4 October 2026}}</ref>

The [[#All-Ireland final|All-Ireland final]] went to two replays for the only time in the history of the competition.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40354421.html|title=Cork v Kilkenny: A renaissance would be welcomed by all|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=7 August 2021|accessdate=17 October 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/1930-1945-rising-tide/a/148675312.html|title=1930-1945 rising tide|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=11 February 2007|accessdate=17 October 2026}}</ref> The second replay was played at [[Croke Park]] in [[Dublin]] on 1 November 1931 between [[Cork GAA|Cork]] and [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]], in what was their [[Cork–Kilkenny hurling rivalry#All-time results|sixth championship meeting overall]] and a first meeting in the All-Ireland final in [[1926 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|five years]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-10076418.html|title=Honours even: supremacy at stake as Rebels and Cats fight for top spot|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=7 September 2004|accessdate=17 October 2026}}</ref> Cork won the match by 5–08 to 3–04 to claim their 11th All-Ireland title overall and a first title in [[1929 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|two years]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2006/0828/208478-corkvkilkenny/|title=Cork v Kilkenny Classics: 1931 SHC final|publisher=RTÉ Sport|date=14 June 2007|accessdate=17 October 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.echolive.ie/corksport/arid-40273667.html|title=Years ending in one have proved to be tough for Cork hurling teams|publisher=Echo Live|date=24 April 2021|accessdate=17 October 2026}}</ref>

Kilkenny's [[Dan Dunne]] was the championship's top scorer with 8–03.

==Championship statistics==

===Scoring===

*Widest winning margin: '''28 points''' 
**Kilkenny 8–8 : Wexford 1–1 (<small>''Leinster quarter-final, 31 May 1931''</small>)
*Most goals in a match: '''10''' 
**Kilkenny 7–2 : Galway 3–1 (<small>''All-Ireland semi-final, 16 August 1931''</small>)
*Most points in a match: '''12''' 
**Kilkenny 1–6 : Cork 1–6 (<small>''All-Ireland final, 6 September 1931''</small>)
**Kilkenny 3–4 : Cork 5–8 (<small>''All-Ireland final second replay, 1 November 1931''</small>)
*Most goals by one team in a match: '''8''' 
**Kilkenny 8–8 : Wexford 1–1 (<small>''Leinster quarter-final, 31 May 1931''</small>)
*Most goals scored by a losing team: '''4''' 
**Laois 4–2 : Kilkenny 4–7 (<small>''Leinster final, 2 August 1931''</small>)
*Most points scored by a losing team: '''6''' 
**Clare 1–6 : Cork 3–4 (<small>''Munster quarter-final, 28 June 1931''</small>)
